uncovered_reasons.note: `+` concatenates the string literal 'Time: ' with the numeric result of (performance.now() - __hopcStart); with a string-typed operand it is string concatenation, which the compiler has no strength-reduced path for (the numeric `-` inside is optimized via type guards, but the enclosing concat stays generic; a number guard on the parenthesized/binary target has no effect)

Strict comparison confSetNext(starterSet, stateNum) === false. The call result is number|false (confSet slots hold conf indices or the initial false sentinel), so neither a number nor a boolean type guard can specialize it; both were tried with no effect.

Receiver l is a pair; `map` is inherited from pair.prototype (155:22:165:2). Tried instance shape guard on l plus prototype shape guard on a full 8-property pair-prototype shape, with map typed closure and with map untyped; also tried shape_binding on pair.prototype at the method-store receiver 239:1:239:15. The prototype-shape half is never established (dryrun: "killed by 1116:17 property read (unknown shape) .map"; prototype guard "no effect"), because pair.prototype is created implicitly by the function declaration and has no bindable object-creation expression, so the inherited slot cannot be fixed.

Closure-target type guard on the callee expression l.map (target function 155:22:165:2) was auto-pruned as matching no IR: the compiler cannot attach a closure identity guard to an inherited member load whose prototype shape cannot be fixed (see the property_load reason).

Loose equality nts[i] == nt. String type guards on both operands, a number guard on the index source, and a boolean guard on the comparison were all tried and had no effect; the array element load itself stays generic (ArrLen guard only types length), so this binary comparison cannot be specialized.

Prototype method read on a pair list (nts.reverse / nts.reverse().toArray). pair instances are shape-bound to a Pair shape {car,cdr} at the completing constructor write, and pair.prototype is shape-bound to a prototype shape listing constructor plus all seven methods in insertion order at pair.prototype.member (the completing method store). A shape guard on nts with prototype shape PairProto was tried both on the defLoop parameter declaration and directly at the 401 receiver; the compiler reports the prototype half as either 'no effect' or 'killed by property read (unknown shape)', i.e. the prototype shape does not reach slot resolution for the inherited method. A closure type guard on the same member expression does optimize the call (confirmed) but leaves the property read itself generic. No further annotation form can resolve the prototype slot here.

The only concrete type guards are primitives; pair/null cannot be described by any single allowed type (and a degenerate null-only guard would make the fast path useless). Guards tried: number|string on both operands, null on the nil side, full primitive union on a and b — all no effect.
